projects.name: ctxlint
projects.tagline: Lint AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / .cursorrules / Copilot instructions: stale paths & scripts, broken @imports, hidden Unicode, secrets, drift.
projects.pain_point: Teams run several AI coding agents, each with its own instruction file. The files rot (renamed paths, dead scripts), drift apart, bloat, and can hide malicious invisible Unicode.
projects.audience: Developers using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot or Gemini CLI
projects.status_reason: Market review 2026-11-20: @yawlabs/ctxlint (39,400/wk) covers a superset of its checks and uses the same name and config file; hidden-Unicode detection is covered by anti-trojan-source (40,758/wk) and package-manager enforcement by only-allow (2.28M/wk). Not published, to avoid name confusion and long-tail noise. See lab/research/2026-11-20-market-review.md.

projects.name: agent-commit-guard
projects.tagline: Keep the secrets your AI coding agent saves out of git: finds passwords and keys in Claude Code allowlists, MCP configs and agent files, auto-fixes them, and blocks commits (agent hook + pre-commit + CI) while any remain.
projects.pain_point: Claude Code's "don't ask again" saves full approved commands, passwords included, to .claude/settings.local.json; Apiiro found 1,122 public copies holding 1,379 secrets (Nov 2026). MCP configs and session transcripts leak the same way, and generic scanners miss passwords inside commands.
projects.audience: Developers and teams using Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI or MCP servers
projects.rename_reason: 2026-11-24: an established PyPI project (ppravdin/agentscrub, 44 releases since 2026-05-07) already uses the name for local agent-log redaction. Renamed before first publish; README credits it.

projects.name: pthscan
projects.tagline: Audit Python startup hooks (.pth / .start) for credential stealers like the LiteLLM and Microsoft agent-framework compromises, without running them. CI Action + agent hook.
projects.pain_point: Malicious PyPI releases (Microsoft agent-framework 1.26.1/1.26.2 on 17 Nov 2026, LiteLLM 1.82.8, the Hades campaign) plant .pth hooks that run a credential stealer on every Python start. Advice is manual find/grep, which drowns in legitimate hooks and misses payloads in imported modules; no packaged tool checks this.
projects.audience: Python developers, CI/CD owners, security teams
